newsitem.title: USA: Daka says restaurant spin-off is taxable.
newsitem.headline: Daka says restaurant spin-off is taxable.

text.p: Daka International Inc said Wednesday the $195 million sale of its contract foodservice business to Compass Group PLC and a related spin-off of its restaurant business will be taxable to shareholders.
Daka said it will treat the transaction as a redemption of its stock.
Daka said Compass will pay stockholders about $85 million through a $7.50 per share cash tender offer. Compass will also spend about $110 million to repay Daka debt.

Before the sale closes, Daka intends to make various contributions of assets and liabilities to Unique Casual Restaurants, Daka said. Daka shareholders of record on June 24 will receive one share of Unique Casual Restaurants for each share of Daka's stock.
For the transaction as a whole, for every one share of Daka stock tendered to Compass, shareholders will receive $7.50 in cash plus one share of Unique Casual Restaurants Inc stock, Daka said.
Unique Casual will apply for listing of its common stock on the Nasdaq exchange, Daka said.
The company said after the spin-off to Compass, Daka's assets will consist only of its contract catering and vending businesses.

Unique Casual Restaurant's will own and operate Daka's restaurant business, consisting primarily of its Fuddruckers and Champps Americana restaurants and its Great Bagel and Coffee business, Daka said. The unit will own, operate and franchise about 250 restaurants with total sales of more than $325 million.
